newsitem.title: USA: U.S. anti-missile missile suffers fourth test failure.
newsitem.headline: U.S. anti-missile missile suffers fourth test failure.

text.p: An advanced anti-missile missile that would protect U.S. troops and allies in a war suffered its fourth test failure on Thursday at White Sands, New Mexico, the U.S. Defence Department said.

A spokesman, Captain Mike Doubleday, said it was too early to assess whether the failure would change plans to put the first of the Theatre High Altitude Area Defence (THAAD) missiles into operation in 2004.

A department statement said the THAAD tested Thursday missed its target, a simulated enemy missile it was supposed to shoot down, but analysis of test monitors will help show what corrections are needed.

The new missile would shoot down enemy missiles much higher and farther from U.S. troops and allied cities than Patriot missiles did in the Gulf War so debris would not fall on the targets as it did then.

The department said the first test failure was blamed on an error in computer-guidance software, the second on a malfunction after booster missile separation and the third on an apparent electrical short that prevented the missile from locking on to its target.
It said those problems have been fixed and Doubleday said he had no preliminary information on what might have caused the fourth failure.
